title: Rollout rehearsal & observability journal
summary: Notes from a dry-run rehearsal of the new canary rollout + observability probes. Focus: UI feature flag gating, rollout metrics capture, and emergency fallback behaviours. This doc is more of a lab notebook than a polished runbook.
notes:
Context:
- Purpose: validate that the rollout micro-surge and the fallback path (auto-failover to model-variant + UI fallback banner) behave within latency SLOs and that analytic events are emitted consistently.
- Scope: frontend flag gating, backend route routing, telemetry pipelines (event enrichment, sampling), and alert sensitivity.

Play-by-play:
- 10:00: quick ingress check. Verified test harness can inject 500 reqs/min with staged header x-redwood-rollout=test-canary.
- 10:12: enabled UI gate (client-side flag). Observed feature flag sync delay ~4s on cold clients, ~100ms on existing sessions. Note: we should instrument flag sync metric per region.
- 10:20: ramp to 1k rps. Backend circuit-breaker tripped in one canary instance after sustained tail-latency (p95) spike to 980ms. Instance recovered after controller restarted (manual).
- 10:27: analytics pipeline showed event duplication for 'ui.rollout.exposed' (2x) for some sessions — root cause likely double-emission from client + gateway shim during slow network.
- 10:40: exercised fallback: toggled to use 'fallback-variant' model and tooltip banner displayed; observed subtle mismatch in token-cost attribution in console (UI shows dedicated vm cost, backend shows hosted).

Notes-to-self / rough thoughts:
- Add client-side de-dupe id for rollout-exposure events (guid per session).
- Move flag sync to use websocket keepalive vs polling (tradeoffs: complexity vs faster propagation).
- Investigate why controller restart required; add graceful restart and health-check probe to reduce manual intervention.
- Consider sampling at gateway for analytics to avoid duplicates downstream rather than reprocessing in pipeline.

Raw timings (important):
- Feature flag cold-sync: 4.1s (median), 6.8s (95th)
- P95 request latency during ramp: control=120ms, canary=620ms -> spike episodes to ~980ms on one host.
- Event pipeline lag: 18s median, 75s 95th (during surge)

Attachments tested:
- test harness script: scripts/rollout_load_test.py
- alert rule stub: /observability/alerts/rollout-p95.json

Open questions:
- What target p95 do we accept for canary in first 5 minutes of ramp? (Is 600ms acceptable?)
- Should we accept small duplication in events if dedupe increases client-side complexity?
